exclusions.B: Then the captain, Neil Pryor, took a stand.
exclusions.C: He had climbed into the roof with a lamp that morning: the rafters were sound, the gale had taken only the sheeting, and the members could repair it themselves for the price of a summer's teas.
exclusions.D: The vote was eleven to two for Pryor's plan.

WV8-P01.4.note: Pryor 'took a stand' by declaring a position against selling, which he then argues and wins a vote on, so 'stand' is a stance, not seating, a stall, a grove, or support given to someone else.

exclusions.A: Anyone who sits on its veranda on a match day is sitting under the work of a village that looked hard at its own building, trusted what it found, and was proved right.
exclusions.B: The roof those members nailed down is still on the pavilion, sixty years and many gales later.
exclusions.D: Anyone who sits on its veranda on a match day is sitting under the work of a village that looked hard at its own building, trusted what it found, and was proved right.
exclusions.E: The roof those members nailed down is still on the pavilion, sixty years and many gales later.

WV8-P01.5.note: The closing sentence openly praises the village for looking hard, trusting what it found and being proved right, which is admiring rather than detached, critical, amused, or regretful.

exclusions.A: He raised nine hundred dollars in Wendle for buckets and waders, and on the first morning forty volunteers waded in behind him to carry mussels from the shrinking shallows to the channel.
exclusions.C: Teo had sketched a wall of sandbags across the cove's mouth, but there was money for one plan, and Kettle's was already moving.
exclusions.D: He raised nine hundred dollars in Wendle for buckets and waders, and on the first morning forty volunteers waded in behind him to carry mussels from the shrinking shallows to the channel.
exclusions.E: Teo had sketched a wall of sandbags across the cove's mouth, but there was money for one plan, and Kettle's was already moving.

WV8-P02.4.note: Kettle gathered money from the town to pay for buckets and waders ('there was money for one plan'), so 'raised' means collected, not increased an existing sum, mentioned, reared, or built.

exclusions.A: Her report lists every volunteer by name, which seems the least such an effort has earned.

exclusions.C: Her report lists every volunteer by name, which seems the least such an effort has earned.

WV8-P02.5.note: The author dwells on the scale of the hand-carried rescue and says the volunteers' effort has earned being named, an admiring judgment rather than a detached, critical, uneasy, or amused one.
